task_instance: Simulate the 'I'm new to Expo, where do I start' flow: scaffold a new Expo app per the shared setup rule (npx create-expo-app@latest), detect the Expo SDK version from package.json as the skill's shared rules require, and verify the project actually builds by producing a bundled export.
tools_used: Bash (node, npm, npx create-expo-app, npx expo export)
evidence: Ran `npx --yes create-expo-app@latest myapp --template blank` in the work directory; it downloaded the blank template and ran `npm install` (464 packages), producing a full Expo project (App.js, app.json, index.js, package.json, node_modules, .git). Verified SDK detection per the skill's shared rule by reading package.json: dependencies.expo = '~57.0.25'. Attempted `npx expo export --platform web`; the default network call to api.expo.dev/cdp.expo.dev was blocked by the sandbox's proxy policy (403, logged in $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status as connect_rejected to api.expo.dev:443 and cdp.expo.dev:443 -- an environment-level allowlist restriction, not a missing capability). Worked around it by setting EXPO_OFFLINE=1 (a supported Expo CLI flag) and installing react-dom@19.2.3 and react-native-web@0.21.1 via plain `npm install` (since `expo install`'s own React Native Directory compatibility check also hit the same blocked host). Re-ran `EXPO_OFFLINE=1 EXPO_NO_TELEMETRY=1 npx expo export --platform web`, which succeeded: 'Web Bundled 7597ms index.js (183 modules)' and wrote dist/index.html, dist/favicon.ico, dist/metadata.json, and dist/_expo/static/js/web/index-8d4f1ec0c7a7266663f1721d987426c2.js (332KB). Confirmed all four output files exist on disk with `find dist -type f` and inspected index.html content. This demonstrates the core router-skill deliverable is reachable in this runtime: Expo project scaffolding, SDK-version detection, and a working, verified build output, all achievable locally without any blocked capability once the documented EXPO_OFFLINE flag was used (device/simulator testing via eas-simulator or physical hardware was out of scope for this router skill's own deliverable and was not attempted).
